newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 10.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The government waits out the farmers' blockade, hoping to point out to all prospective strikers that it has no margins to diverge from the economic policy already announced. This week will see strike action from teachers, doctors and civil aviation employees. The danger of a general paralysis of the country looms large.

--Greek and Turkish businessmen take steps towards joint cooperation at their two-day meeting in Athens. The first step will be a regular half-yearly meeting. Joint business cooperation will have a positive effect on the resolution of political differences, speakers say.
--Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos and Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos agree on foreign policy but disagree with Prime Minister Costas Simitis's handling of the Cyprus flyovers moratorium.
--Opposition parties warn Simitis that he may have to face unpleasant surprises at the Dublin EU summit regarding the issue of the name of the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia.
--Engineers say the Athens Metro will not be completed till after 2001 as state and construction company representatives prepare to meet this week.

--An open letter to Simitis calls on him to make a move to defuse the crisis over the continuing farmers' blockade and coming strike action by others. Evros and Macedonia begin to see empty stalls in central markets.
--Greece's leading homeopath George Vithoulkas receives the 'Right Livelihood Award' - the self-styled 'alternate Nobel' - in Sweden.

--Factories in northern Greece and Thessaly face serious problems as road and rail links remain blocked while even hospitals have begun to feel the pinch with medical supplies running out. Exporters in northern Greece meanwhile are preparing to sue.
--A 25-year-old man went hunting for his estranged wife in hospital after attacking her with a knife, shooting down 20-year-old Despina and her mother in a hospital ward.
--Ruling party PASOK prepares to implement a strategic plan to dismantle road blocks in various locations gradually and isolate militant farmers in Larissa.
--Conservative opposition New Democracy leader Miltiades Evert lashes out at Simitis in Parliament last night, accusing him of 'inaccuracies' and of being "a simple bureaucrat".
